# Maintenance receiver observations, 2026-10-24

Source: `a95225f9481013aeffd885ac9c4985a63237d6d4`.
Contract: [0043/HMT](../../../designs/harness-maintenance.md).
Guide: [harnessctl maintenance](../../../../cmd/harnessctl/maintenance.md).
[Sanitized receipt](receipt.json) contains only scoped counts and public code/binary identities.
GT9A remains in progress. These observations do not qualify live consent or installed hooks.

The final binary was built from a working tree based on `afe07d5`. A 22-file
before/after manifest, including the Go entry point and Swift source, is stable
and matches the source commit byte-for-byte. It does not claim bit-reproducible builds.
Other inputs remain unchanged from that base. Private receipts retain exact tool,
source and binary identities, raw synthetic state and failed attempts.

The native-clock trial performs init/check/end, repeat-init and valid-recovery holds,
forbidden advisory preparation, foreign-controller recovery after corrupted CURRENT,
original-controller locked recovery and locked-origin rearm preparation. Every call
has zero native approval attempts/invocations/completions and false signature flags.
The foreign controller cannot replace BINDING. Preparing rearm does not unlock it.

## Performance scope

Final ordinary config comparison preserves all four check/explain JSON/text outputs
byte-for-byte. Nine alternating before/after pairs have medians 7.037ms/7.411ms,
ratio 1.0532, within the predeclared 1.25 limit. The earlier unchanged-help comparison
also passed and remains retained. These are process-level synthetic observations,
not token, cost or production benefit measurements.

Nine final armed receiver checks have p50 163.296ms and p95/max 241.406ms.
The prior retake had p50 100.426ms and p95/max 115.578ms. Both are retained;
the final retake binds the last help-text change as well as the receiver source.
The host had concurrent work. Each check starts two native clock processes and
commits one observed-clock state transition. Physical syscall/IO counts were not
instrumented. Installed dispatcher adoption needs an explicit traffic/latency budget;
these timings do not establish an acceptable hook budget or approval latency.

## Repaired failures and retained unknowns

- Initial Swift plan validation expected integer UTC values where Go emitted RFC3339.
  Actual Go-to-Swift qualification caught it. The final parser and durable opt-in test agree.
- Recovery originally allowed replacement authority during ambiguity. Immutable BINDING,
  exact resume evidence and unused-slot checks close the reviewed source path and actual
  foreign-controller binary case. Missing/corrupt established binding still holds.
- Preparation originally trusted ambient scratch and then only a private leaf. The
  selected root and its complete protected ancestor identity chain are now checked.
  This is a protected namespace prerequisite, not a same-UID or administrator sandbox.
- The original preview hung through its timeout. A private phase-instrumented baseline
  reached the modal loop and fired cancellation but did not dispatch it or return before
  an 8s outer kill. With a shortened 2s diagnostic deadline, the fix dispatched through
  AppKit modal/default modes and returned canceled in 2.256s. Final production EOF probes
  pass. This diagnostic is distinct from a full 120s production-deadline trial.
- One intermediate SDK compile failed on a throwing short-circuit expression. The final
  nested guard compiles. Expiry checks now bracket review, authentication and signing.
- One parent trial expected incomplete exit 2 for locked `rearm_required`; HMT's known
  policy denial is exit 1. The fresh independent oracle follows that contract. No control
  was weakened. An initial CUE filename-format invocation failed; exact bytes were then
  checked as JSON under both versions. All failed receipts are retained privately.
- Computer-use could not bind either the raw or temporary packaged preview. No screenshot,
  attended task, keyboard, screen-reader or visual acceptance is claimed.
- The skill's bundled Python validator lacked PyYAML. Ruby parsed its frontmatter,
  local references resolved, and the independent explicit skill/guide trial ran.
  Automatic harness discovery and live native-consent routing were not qualified.

The additive `Harness maintenance observations` workflow compiles the SDK and runs
synthetic receiver/CUE/syntax tests. It never calls `approve` or `preview`. Source publication produced three terminal startup refusals: [HMT](https://github.com/GeoffMillerAZ/agentic-kit/actions/runs/40149714071), [CI](https://github.com/GeoffMillerAZ/agentic-kit/actions/runs/40149714136), and [native observations](https://github.com/GeoffMillerAZ/agentic-kit/actions/runs/40149714057). All eight jobs ran zero steps. Their annotations confirm refusal before startup, so hosted execution remains unknown. Private account diagnostics are retained privately; no billing or host policy was changed. Workflow source alone is not execution proof.
Live Secure Enclave enrollment/user-presence signing, attended approval UI, Windows/
Linux native approval, power-loss durability, global hook control, actual dispatcher
interception and production economics remain unqualified. GT9..11 and the full goal
remain open. No installation, real authentication, model call or global settings change
was performed.

Publication used normal hooks: source pre-push validation and isolated Fathom verification both passed. Only the owned worker worktrees/topic branches were removed after all changed paths were present in published source or retained as superseded versions in checksum-verified private archives. The source Git bundle and terminal helper jobs are backed up before cleanup.
